editorNote: Cheaper small models, bigger machine mathematics and the first bruise on it, and a pair of open-source tools that ask little of you.

stories.headline: Anthropic ships Claude Haiku 5.5 at $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens
stories.summary: Haiku 5.5 launched October 7 at $0.10 input and $0.50 output per million tokens for prompts up to 100k, about 75% cheaper to run than Haiku 4.5 by Anthropic's account. It scores 72.4% on OSWorld 2.1 (offline subset) against 15.7% for Haiku 4.5, and trails Sonnet 5.5 across the listed benchmarks.
stories.whyItMatters: The small tier is now far cheaper and, per vendor benchmarks, much closer to Sonnet-class on agentic tasks; Sonnet 5.5 cache reads were also halved.

stories.headline: OpenAI's batch of AI-written maths results loses three papers to a sign error
stories.summary: OpenAI's math repository withdrew three Hodge-conjecture-related manuscripts on October 7 after a sign error invalidated a stabilization-trace cancellation argument that the others also relied on. Scott Aaronson had called the release of roughly 372 results a 'Mathocalypse', noting only some come with Lean certificates and that the model solved about 5% of problems attempted.
stories.whyItMatters: The first public retraction shows why verification, not generation, is now the bottleneck for AI-produced proofs.

stories.headline: Docker Agent: declarative YAML multi-agent runtime, Apache-2.0
stories.summary: Docker's open-source agent builder defines agent teams in YAML, supports any MCP server and providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and local models, and can push and pull agents via OCI registries.
stories.whyItMatters: It treats agents as versioned, shareable artefacts like container images.

stories.headline: ascii.rest offers 208 dependency-free animated ASCII pieces for the web
stories.summary: The MIT-licensed collection ships each piece as a small TypeScript module usable in HTML, React, Next.js or Astro, and plays in a terminal via 'npx ascii.rest donut'.
stories.whyItMatters: Purely decorative, but a tidy example of the zero-dependency widget.
